summary.short: North Carolina HB 591 (2024) creates sexual extortion offenses under G.S. 14-202.7: a Class F felony for adults and, for minors, a Class 1 misdemeanor (first offense) or Class F felony (repeat). Aggravated sexual extortion against a minor or a person with a disability by an adult is a Class E felony. The act extends the material and image definitions to algorithm- or AI-created or altered depictions of identifiable individuals and adds identifiable-minor material to sexual exploitation offenses. It adds G.S. 14-190.17C, extends registrant premises restrictions, requires entities receiving certain reports to forward them to the Cyber Tip Line, and gives private-image disclosure victims a civil action with liquidated damages of $1,000 per day or $10,000 plus punitive damages and fees. Effective 1 December 2024 for offenses committed on or after that date.
summary.long: HB 591 (2024) creates sexual extortion offenses under G.S. 14-202.7: a Class F felony for adults and, for minors, a Class 1 misdemeanor (first offense) or Class F felony (repeat). Aggravated sexual extortion against a minor or a person with a disability by an adult is a Class E felony. The act extends the material and image definitions to algorithm- or AI-created or altered depictions of identifiable individuals and adds identifiable-minor material to sexual exploitation offenses. It adds G.S. 14-190.17C, extends registrant premises restrictions, requires entities receiving certain reports to forward them to the Cyber Tip Line, and gives private-image disclosure victims a civil action with liquidated damages of $1,000 per day or $10,000 plus punitive damages and fees. Effective 1 December 2024 for offenses committed on or after that date.

notes: Amending sections Sec. 2(a)-(d), 2(f), 3 and 4 say 'reads as rewritten' but the printed text shows no marking of changed words, so changed text cannot be isolated from restated text here. Definition conflict: Sec. 1 G.S. 14-202.7(a)(6) defines 'Minor' as under 18 with no marriage or emancipation exception, while G.S. 14-190.13(3) (as rewritten by Sec. 2(a)) defines 'Minor' as under 18 and not married or judicially emancipated. Sec. 4 quotes G.S. 14-190.5A(a)(4) and (5) as repealed by Session Laws 2017-93; that repeal is not made by this act. Sec. 3(b) omits a comma in the list 'G.S. 14-190.17 G.S. 14-190.17A, or G.S. 14-190.17C'. Sec. 5 makes the act effective December 1, 2024, applying to offenses committed on or after that date. Entities are limited to named bodies; the reporting entities in G.S. 14-208.15A(e) are an unnamed class and are not listed.
